output.summary: KEP-2450 proposed removing kube-proxy's dependence on the pod cluster CIDR in iptables and ipvs rules, replacing it with node-local pod traffic signals (node podCIDR, pod interface prefix, or physdev matching). The KEP is recorded as implemented, stage stable.
output.rationale: Kube-proxy's iptables and ipvs rules referenced the cluster CIDR for pods in several places, which tied pod IP allocation to service routing. The proposal argues that tracking node-local pod traffic is enough to identify cluster-originated traffic, so allocators can change without touching service rules. The main drawback noted is a relaxed accept rule for ESTABLISHED,RELATED packets, which holds only if pod traffic is routed at the node boundary on every node.

alternatives.option: Keep referencing the pod cluster CIDR in iptables and ipvs rules
alternatives.why_not: The sources say this coupling prevents decoupling pod IP management and allocation strategies from service management and routing, which is the stated goal.

alternatives.option: Use -s node.podCIDR to identify cluster-originated traffic
alternatives.why_not: Listed as one of several equivalent alternatives in the proposal; the sources do not say why it was chosen over the others.

alternatives.option: Use --in-interface prefix+ to match pod interfaces
alternatives.why_not: Listed as an equivalent alternative; the sources do not record a specific reason it was not selected.
Offered for kubenet when node podCIDR is not wanted; the sources do not say it was rejected.

evidence.quote: This enhancement proposes ways to achieve similar goals without tracking the pod cluster CIDR to do so.
Not having to depend on the cluster pod CIDR for routing service traffic would effectively de-couple pod IP management and allocation strategies from service management and routing.
The main caveat in this KEP is the relaxation of the accept rule for "ESTABLISHED,RELATED" packets.
https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2867 retroactively declared this beta since that's where this ultimately ended up during 1.21.
It landed after https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/2672 (which made PRR required for implementable), but since it landed as implemented, it skipped PRR
